play.definition: Gap scheme with playside down blocks and a crack block from the backside receiver to seal the defensive end, optionally with a backside guard pull

action.label: Ball Carry
action.definition: Any action by an offensive player who has possession of the football and is attempting to advance it downfield, including running, scrambling after a reception, or after a fumble recovery.

action.label: Ball Snap
action.definition: The action of the center (or occasionally another player) legally putting the ball into play by handing or tossing it between their legs to a backfield player (typically the quarterback) to initiate a down.

action.label: Crack Block
action.definition: A block executed by a wide receiver or tight end on an inside defender (often a linebacker or defensive end) who is lined up inside of them, typically on a run play designed to go outside. The receiver 'cracks back' on the defender.

action.label: None
action.definition: A temporal label used when the player is visible but is not performing any defined football action in the action taxonomy during the annotated interval.

action.label: Pre Snap
action.definition: The period before the snap when players are set in formation and no active play has begun.

action.label: Pull Block
action.definition: An offensive lineman's action of pulling from their original position on the line of scrimmage to block a defender at a different point of attack, often in a different gap or on the perimeter.

action.label: Snap Receive
action.definition: The action of the quarterback securing the ball from the center’s snap to initiate the play.

action.label: Toss
action.definition: A type of handoff where the quarterback 'tosses' or pitches the ball underhand laterally to a running back or other offensive player who is often moving parallel to the line of scrimmage, typically to the outside.
